transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-17
Start: 15:30 PT
Duration: 54 minutes (recording appears continuous)
Attendees: Nikhil Rao, Lena Ortiz, Marcus Lee (Redwood); Priya Desai, Tom Weller, Marta Ruiz, Leo Chan (AstraNova)

Summary:
Redwood run-through of SOC 2 Type II evidence availability, ISO 27001 scope, trust portal access patterns, RBAC/SSO integration (SAML + SCIM), audit log retention and export, and KMS options including BYOK and HSM integration. Customer clarified EU residency requirement for production; asked about dedicated vs hosted and fallback for latency-sensitive endpoints. Agreed next steps: share reports, RBAC mapping template, schedule SSO test and trust portal walkthrough.

Topics covered:
- Reports available (SOC2 Type II, ISO27001 cert, penetration test summaries)
- Trust portal / evidence access and RBAC for auditors
- SSO / SCIM provisioning and RBAC role mapping
- Audit logs retention, exports, and tamper evidence
- KMS integration: BYOK, HSM support, key rotation cadence and attestation
- Data residency and dedicated capacity options

Transcript (timestamps approximate, auto transcript with occasional errors):
[00:00] Nikhil: all right folks thanks for carving out time today we're gonna do a quick posture review and then walk through the trust portal and SSO flows, lena will cover the RBAC details, marcus will cover logs and kms.
[00:27] Priya: thanks yeah high level for us we want to validate the SOC2/ISO evidence is accessible to our auditors and make sure we can enforce EU-only data, and also how keys are managed because our regulator requires HSM backed keys.
[00:48] Lena: yeah totally, on the reports side we have a redacted SOC 2 Type II we can share, and an ISO 27001 scope doc. the trust portal exposes per-control evidence attachments, control mappings are csv exportable.
[01:13] Tom: quick q, does the trust portal let us create auditor accounts with read-only access? we need to give external auditors sight but no ability to change configs.
[01:27] Marcus: yes you can create auditor role, read-only, time-boxed access, and we log all access events. logs include user id, action, ip, and object. retention by default is 90 days on hosted but we can export or lengthen retention for enterprise plans.
[01:49] Marta: 90 days is short for us — our policy needs 365 days for audit trails, is that something we can configure?
[02:01] Nikhil: on Dedicated or Private deployments we support longer retention; for Hosted we can add log retention add-ons or push to your SIEM via S3/BigQuery exports.
[02:18] Priya: okay that's helpful. how about KMS, we need BYOK with HSM and remote attestation. any customers using Azure Key Vault or AWS CloudHSM?
[02:32] Lena: we support BYOK integrations with AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and Azure Key Vault. for HSM-backed keys we accept CloudHSM or Azure Dedicated HSM. remote attestation depends on provider; we also support a bring-your-key workflow where the master key lives in your HSM and tokens are provided to the service.
[02:57] Leo: is the encryption at rest model envelope encryption? are tokens stored in KV cache? just trying to map flows.
[03:09] Marcus: yes envelope encryption; data encrypted with per-tenant data key, which is wrapped by your master KMS key. small note — kv cache here refers to model KV cache, not keyvault. sometimes the auto transcript spelled it out as 'K V cache' which is confusing.
[03:29] Nikhil: (laughs) yes we've seen that.
[03:32] [crosstalk] Speaker 5: sorry can you repeat the rotation cadence?
[03:38] Lena: rotation is configurable — default rotation for data keys is 90 days, master keys follow your KMS policy. we provide audit logs for key usage, key-wrap operations are logged with request ID.
[03:55] Tom: how does RBAC work across multiple teams — we have dozens of apps using inference, need role separation between dev, qa, and security.
[04:09] Lena: roles are hierarchical; you can define organization roles and project roles. SCIM provisioning supports groups, we map SCIM groups to role templates. you can also use inline role overrides for specific routes. sample template is in the RBAC guide we'll send.
[04:29] Marta: and SSO providers — we use Okta and Google Workspace, is SCIM provisioning tested?
[04:36] Marcus: yes Okta and GSuite tested; SCIM patch semantics are supported but the exact claims mapping can vary, we'll share the SCIM schema and example mappings.
[04:52] Priya: for compliance evidence we need to know the exact controls mapped to SOC2 Trust Services Criteria and ISO Annex A controls, is that exported?
[05:05] Lena: control mapping is in the portal, each control links to evidence attachments; exports include control id, description, owner, evidence file link, and timestamps. small caveat — sometimes third-party pen-test reports are redacted and show as references.
[05:23] Tom: what's the process if an auditor requests raw logs — do we provide CSV exports?
[05:30] Marcus: yes CSV or parquet. we can also set up a one-time S3 export for the audit period. all exports are hashed and checksummed; we record that in the evidence entry.
[05:46] Priya: about data residency — we want eu-only for prod; can you guarantee EU region processing and storage?
[05:55] Nikhil: for Hosted we deploy in the region you select and guarantee at-rest and in-transit within that region, but note that control plane metadata may be in our control plane region. If full EU isolation is required we recommend Private deployment with customer-managed control plane.
[06:18] Leo: can we do a hybrid? dev in hosted US, prod in EU?
[06:24] Lena: yes that's a supported pattern, routing policies pin requests by project to specific region/model instance. we'll show you how to create a policy for that.
[06:36] [10m mark noise; partial audio drop]
[06:50] Marcus: on dedicated vs hosted tradeoffs: Dedicated gives you predictable throughput and better unit controls for logs and key material. Hosted gives faster onboarding but some enterprise controls might be limited without private.
[07:05] Tom: latency sensitive endpoints — if we pin to EU region will we get any penalty for cold starts?
[07:12] Lena: cold start tradeoffs depend on model size and instance type, we also support warm pools and async batching. for low latency models we recommend smaller sequence lengths and model quantization; Optimize can recommend quantization profiles per workload.
[07:35] Priya: can Redwood provide the list of endpoints used for IP allowlisting for our firewall?
[07:41] Nikhil: yes, we'll send a static IP list for the EU region and documentation for firewall rules — note some services still rely on managed endpoints for control plane tasks.
[07:56] Marta: audit of vendor access — do you maintain an access log for Redwood engineers? who can access customer evidence?
[08:07] Marcus: access by Redwood staff is strictly controlled; we have RBAC, SSO for our own staff, and access logs with justification. for Private deployments you can eliminate vendor access entirely. we also support JIT just-in-time sessions with approval flows.
[08:25] [08:30] Priya: are there certifications for data centers hosting the EU region?
[08:34] Lena: the cloud providers have their certifications; we can provide the list of regions and underlying provider attestations as part of the evidence pack.
[08:45] Tom: curious about penetration testing — do you run independent pen tests and share summaries?
[08:52] Nikhil: yes annual third-party pen testing, we share executive summaries and remediation timelines; full reports are redacted for customer distribution but auditors can request more detail under NDA.
[09:05] Leo: one more technical — for KMS, do you support key wrapping with asymmetric keys or only symmetric CMKs?
[09:12] Marcus: primary support is symmetric CMKs but we can use asymmetric keys for specific flows; depends on KMS provider and HSM support. we'll check specifics for Azure Dedicated HSM.
[09:27] [pause] Speaker 5: sorry unclear, you said control exports include timestamps and checksums?
[09:33] Lena: yes each evidence file has an sha256 and upload timestamp; the evidence ledger tracks changes.
[09:40] Priya: how are change requests tracked if an evidence item is updated? we need full history.
[09:46] Marcus: the portal keeps version history for evidence attachments and control mapping changes, you can export the change log for audit purposes.
[09:56] Nikhil: ok wanted to pivot to scheduling — next week would work to do a hands-on SSO test?
[10:04] Priya: week of 3/23 looks good, prefer mornings CET.
[10:10] Nikhil: great we'll propose a few slots.
[10:14] [11:00] Tom: are there any known limitations in the SCIM implementation we should watch for?
[11:20] Lena: we handle group membership, but large group syncs can be slow; we recommend provisioning via group-of-groups or scoping to specific groups to keep the payload small. also some identity providers differ on custom attribute mapping which requires a one-off mapping.
[11:45] Marta: about evidentiary chain of custody, does the portal do tamperproofing?
[11:52] Marcus: we write an immutable event to an append-only ledger internally and store file checksums; for enterprise customers we can provide signed manifests.
[12:06] Priya: can we run a demo of the portal and show how to export control matrices?
[12:12] Lena: yes we can — demo will show control list, evidence attachments, export csv, and how to invite auditor accounts. we'll demo SCIM provisioning in a test Okta tenant.
[12:28] Leo: small note — in our environment we have strict egress rules, will the trust portal still be reachable?
[12:36] Marcus: for restricted networks we can use private deployment or peering; for hosted we provide static IP allowlist and VPC peering in dedicated.
[12:49] [13:10] Priya: cost question — any add-on pricing for longer log retention and evidence export?
[13:18] Nikhil: yes longer retention and premium evidence retention are add-ons or part of dedicated plans; we'll include rough pricing in the follow-up email.
[13:31] Tom: request: can you include a sample control mapping for common controls mapping SOC2 CC6 to ISO A.9 etc?
[13:40] Lena: yes the template includes a control matrix with mapping examples.
[13:46] Priya: ok let's capture next steps.
[13:51] Nikhil: recap — we'll send SOC2 redacted report and ISO certificate, RBAC/SCIM guide, static ip list, and propose SSO test slots. Marcus/Lena to run portal demo week of 3/23. customer to confirm EU-only residency and provide list of systems.
[14:15] Marta: thanks all that was helpful.
[14:20] [audio artifact — faint hum for 5s]
[14:30] Speaker 5: quick clarification on evidence — do you support annotating evidence with control owner names?
[14:37] Lena: yes owner field is available, and you can add comments and attachments per evidence item.
[14:45] Priya: final question around legal / procurement — do you produce SOC2 bridge letters for mid-year audits?
[14:54] Nikhil: we can provide a bridge letter in some cases; depends on timing and scope. we'll surface policy in the follow-up.
[15:06] [closing] Nikhil: great, we'll follow up with the artifacts and book the SSO test. thanks everyone.

End of recording.
